step2_progress_discovery.summary: progress = ram[0x006C] | ram[0x0065]<<8 (a 16-bit LE fine-x/screen pair). Confirmed via action-conditioned delta correlation + dense per-step trace inspection + cross-segment wrap coupling + a two-life-length saturation probe. See rejected_candidates for the false positives the DISCOVERY LORE tests specifically caught.
step2_progress_discovery.why_the_opening_is_hard: The captured start state drops Arthur directly adjacent to an already-active zombie (visually confirmed via rendered frames). Every pure scripted hold (right/left/noop/B-mash/right+A/right+B) dies at ~step 70-130 near spawn, so the classic 'hold right N steps, hold left N steps' controlled probe only samples a tiny, combat-dominated window. Real multi-screen forward distance only appears in lucky random-restart rollouts.

rejected_candidates.reason: free-running frame clock: climbs at an IDENTICAL ~1.3/step rate under NOOP, RIGHT, and LEFT (byte-for-byte identical sequences over 34-128 step controlled probes AND from an independent mid-level save-state) -- the exact MM2 $001C trap the lore names.

0x05C0 SATURATES (caps ~224-250 across 108 independent long segments) -- the Kirby camera-clamp signature; 0x06C2 is direction-independent (identical net under LEFT and RIGHT) and its dense trace is non-monotone noise (254,22,22,22,16,22,76,254,22,94,22 across a visually-confirmed-monotone ladder) -- an enemy/object-slot artifact, not position.
all climb at the SAME ~1.3/step rate identically under NOOP and RIGHT from an independent mid-level save-state (34-step exact match) -- more free-running clocks.

one-shot combat/collision EVENT FLAGS: a single large transition (e.g. 204->0) at a fixed early step under RIGHT, dead flat before and after, absent entirely under LEFT within the same budget -- not a continuous track.
mirrored pair, but only ONE transition (255->96) in an entire 270-step real-progress segment, right at its end -- looks like a death/transition-adjacent flag, not a per-step position.

winner.discovery_method: Action-conditioned delta correlation: mean per-step signed RAM delta split by whether the taken action contained 'right' / 'left' / neither, pooled across 243 independent death-restarted rollouts (30000 steps, single worker, right/A/B-biased sampling). 0x003D, 0x0064, and 0x006C (near-mirror addresses) surfaced with mean delta +1.1 to +1.2 under right, -0.66 to -0.82 under left, and ~0.01-0.23 under neither.
winner.noop_flat_test: 0x006C: net=0 over 73 NOOP-only steps from the true start state (dead flat, all 73 values identically 0).
winner.hold_right_test: 0x006C: net=67 over 128 steps, mono=0.66; dense trace shows a real walking signature (smooth +1..+6/step climbs, a plateau where Arthur is blocked, then a clean retreat/knockback decline) -- NOT a linear clock.
winner.hold_left_test: 0x006C: net=0 over 70 steps (flat, identical to NOOP). Interpreted as a LEFT-BOUNDARY CLAMP, not a rejection: the start state is the very first screen of Stage 1 -- there is nowhere further left to go, so a real position byte SHOULD be pinned here under LEFT.
winner.gameplay_locked_wrap_test: Dense per-step trace (not just checkpoints) of 0x006C's mirror 0x003D over the 270-step visually-confirmed-monotone segment shows a CLEAN wrap: ...245, 251, 254, 1, 4, 10, 13... (254->1, no intermediate garbage). Cross-validated the coupled high byte across the full 243-segment corpus (28 independent wrap events of the lo byte): 0x0065 increments by exactly +1 in 28/28 (100%) when paired with lo=0x006C (vs 28/33=85% for the 0x003D mirror and 21-29/33 for other candidate high bytes) -- the cleanest lo/hi pair found.
winner.saturation_test: PASS (does not cap). The longest captured single life (271 steps, independent seed) crosses TWO lo-byte wraps -- hi (0x0065) reaches a sustained value of 2, filtered for the 1-frame glitch below -- without the value capping the way 0x05C0 does (saturates ~224-250) or resetting the way the pre-existing 0x005D does. The actual SOLVE run (6 min, 3 workers, count selection) drove the max_gx_in_max_area frontier to 3327, ~13x past a single lo-byte wrap (256), confirming continued accumulation deep into the search, not a camera-window cap.
winner.known_artifact: 0x0065 spikes to 255 for exactly ONE frame (self-correcting the very next frame) during the first-hit/invincibility-init routine (~step 20-26 in every trajectory observed, i.e. RAM-address reuse coincident with the armor-loss animation), which would otherwise read as a huge bogus progress value for that single frame. Guarded via progress_cap: 8000 in the written solve: section (GenericGame's existing transition-frame-garbage guard).

step2_y_discovery.method: Differential probing: identical save-state, one branch held jump(A) in bursts, the other held pure NOOP; per-byte |diff| between the two branches at matching time steps ranked candidates.
step2_y_discovery.caveat_HONEST: Could NOT verify a NOOP-flat Y from a genuinely safe stance -- the pinned opening means every state we could reach is combat-adjacent, so an involuntary knockback-into-air from the nearby zombie fires on almost the same schedule whether or not A is pressed (0x021B showed the identical rise-peak-decline arc under a pure-NOOP run AND under an A-burst run once from that specific pinned start). 0x021B is used as a PROVISIONAL height proxy: real 0-255 dynamic range, a bounded ballistic (rise-then-fall, not unbounded) envelope consistent with real airborne physics (self-jump or knockback-launch), clearly divergent from a matched-NOOP baseline when probed from a safer save-state (post-first-kill). Recommend re-verifying from a cleaner mid-stage save-state once one is captured.

honest_caveats: Y (0x021B) is provisional: could not verify NOOP-flatness from a genuinely safe stance because none was reachable from this start state within the investigation budget; it is a real, wide-range, jump/knockback-responsive height signal but conflates voluntary jumps with involuntary knockback launches.

level_key is an empty coverage baseline -- no real stage-clear signal exists yet; a future pass should look for a stage/area-index byte once deep-arrival save-states from THIS solve's archive make an actual 1-A->1-B transition reachable.

progress (0x006C/0x0065) was validated on a LEFT-flat / boundary-clamp basis rather than a true LEFT-negative basis, because the captured start state sits at the stage's own left boundary. This is architecturally sound (nowhere further left exists) but is a weaker form of the textbook reversibility test than a mid-level LEFT-decreases check would be.
